title: Understanding Drainage Slope and Flow Velocity
description: Proper pitch on horizontal drainage piping is critical for maintaining adequate water velocity to carry solid waste without leaving deposits behind. If a pipe lacks sufficient slope, liquid moves too slowly, causing solids to settle and accumulate into blockages over time. Conversely, excessive pitch can allow liquid to run off too quickly, potentially leaving solid waste stranded in the line. Plumbers must reference local building codes for required minimum slopes relative to pipe diameter to achieve optimal self-scouring velocity throughout the drainage system.

Understanding Drainage Slope and Flow Velocity

Proper pitch on horizontal drainage piping is critical for maintaining adequate water velocity to carry solid waste without leaving deposits behind. If a pipe lacks sufficient slope, liquid moves too slowly, causing solids to settle and accumulate into blockages over time. Conversely, excessive pitch can allow liquid to run off too quickly, potentially leaving solid waste stranded in the line. Plumbers must reference local building codes for required minimum slopes relative to pipe diameter to achieve optimal self-scouring velocity throughout the drainage system.
